summary:
## The Everyday Makeup Philosophy
This routine is designed to be a quick, 15-minute process for a polished, put-together look that is flattering and natural. The core idea is to enhance your features without looking like you're wearing a ton of makeup, prioritizing lightweight products and strategic application.

## Base Application Sequence
- **Tinted Moisturizer**: Start with a tinted moisturizer instead of foundation for a more skin-like finish. Apply a **thin, even layer**, ensuring the product is a **non-pilling** formula for a smooth canvas.
- **Cream Bronzer**: Use a cream bronzer that **melts into the skin**. Apply with a dense brush to place the color, then blend with a fluffier brush for an airbrushed effect.
- **Cream Blush**: A **pigmented, buildable cream blush** adds a healthy flush. Apply straight from the stick for intensity or from the back of the hand for a softer look.
- **Concealer**: Opt for a **medium-coverage, thin-consistency concealer** for a natural finish under the eyes that brightens without creasing.

> [!TIP]
> After applying all cream products, spritz your face with a **setting spray**. This helps all the layers melt together, look more natural, and last longer throughout the day.

## Eye & Powder Techniques
- **Simple Eyes**: Create an effortless eye look with a **neutral matte shade** in the crease, a **sheer shimmer topper** on the lid, and a smudged 'baby wing' using a **brown eyeliner pencil**.
- **Waterline Trick**: Apply a **nude or white eyeliner** only to the **center of your lower waterline**. This creates the illusion of bigger, more awake eyes.
- **Strategic Powdering**: Use different powders for different parts of the face. 
  - A **finely-milled blurring powder** pressed into the under-eyes and smile lines with a powder puff prevents creasing.
  - A **luminous finishing powder** used lightly on the rest of the face sets makeup while preserving a natural glow.
- **Layering Powders**: Gently sweep **powder bronzer and blush** over their cream counterparts to set them and add a bit more dimension and longevity.

## The Perfect Nude Lip
Achieve a custom, flattering nude lip with this three-step technique:
1.  **Line & Define**: Overline lips slightly with a neutral lip liner and fill in the outer corners.
2.  **Add Tinted Balm**: Apply a hydrating tinted balm all over the lips.
3.  **Create a Nude Center**: Take a **tiny amount of concealer** on your fingertip and press it into the center of your lips. This lightens the color and creates a custom nude shade that perfectly matches your skin tone.

## Featured Products
- **Base**: NARS Pure Radiant Tinted Moisturizer, Saie Sun Melt Cream Bronzer, Westman Atelier Baby Cheeks Blush, Armani Luminous Silk Concealer.
- **Eyes**: Makeup by Mario Master Mattes Palette, Victoria Beckham Lid Luster, Laura Mercier Caviar Eyeliner Pencil.
- **Powders**: Pat McGrath Blurring Under-Eye Powder, Hourglass Ambient Lighting Palette, NARS Laguna Bronzing Powder.
- **Lips**: Victoria Beckham Lip Definer, Ilia Balmy Tint Hydrating Lip Balm.

## Intro: A Quick & Easy Everyday Routine

To be honest, on an everyday basis I do not have a ton of time to do my makeup, so I created this routine for when you have like 15 minutes but you want to look really good. Okay, this is the ultimate everyday makeup routine that will just honestly look flattering on anyone.

If you want to know how I achieve this look, keep on watching. But before we get into it, don't forget to give this video a big thumbs up and subscribe to my channel. It really helps me out a lot. But yeah, let's get right into it.

## Base: Applying Tinted Moisturizer

I like to always start with my base, and when I'm doing my everyday makeup I typically like to reach for a tinted moisturizer instead of a foundation. Today I'm using one of my favorites, I'm using the NARS Pure Radiant Tinted Moisturizer in the shade St. Moritz Light Zero. And the reason I like to reach for a tinted moisturizer rather than a foundation is for every day, I just want to look like myself, but I want to look better. I want to look good, I want to look put together. I don't really want to look like I'm wearing a ton of makeup. And honestly, I just feel like tinted moisturizers are kind of slept on these days. I just kind of feel like I'm wearing a mask when I wear foundation, although there are some good ones, don't get me wrong. 

But as you can see, I'm just applying a very even, thin layer of this. I really don't want to go for full coverage at this stage. We're going to kind of add our coverage very selectively later on. But for now, just make sure you blend your Tinted Moisturizer in really good. Make sure it's a nice thin even layer, no brush streaks. Just take your time with the base. Something I really love about this tinted moisturizer is that it never pills on me, and this is something really important because if a base product is peeling all the time, it just ruins your entire makeup and it's just not worth it. So I really vet my base products. This one's never let me down.

## Brush Recommendation & Discount Code

To blend that out, I used my Hourglass foundation brush. I'm always using this brush, I cannot recommend it enough, but I always forget to mention I have a discount code with Hourglass. So if you want to use it, save some money, it is Amanda10. All of my discount codes are always listed down below in the description, so if you ever want to know what I'm using, just check down there. All the information will be there for you.

## Warming Up with Cream Bronzer

Now I'm going in with bronzer, and some things for me just don't change. I've been using this bronzer forever, but it is so good. This is the Saie Sun Melt Natural Cream Bronzer. I use the shade Fair Bronze, and I've been using this bronzer for a very long time. I actually hit pan in it, you can hardly see it, but she has been very well loved. And I've said this before, but bronzer can be one of those steps that like takes longer than it needs to. And when I'm doing my quick everyday makeup, I need my bronzer just to like melt in and blend itself out, and that is what this does. I use my Refy brush to apply this. I use the denser side to pack the color on my skin, and then once I've got the product placed how I want it to, I blend it out with the dual fiber, more fluffy side for a very airbrushed finish. And it always looks so good and takes me like no time. And it's a clean product, so we love that.

## Adding a Pop of Cream Blush

Blush is one of my favorite steps of my entire makeup routine. I love it so much, and these quickly have become one of my favorite blushes. These are by Westman Atelier, this is their Baby Cheeks Cream Blush. I'm using the shade Chouchette. These are just so pigmented and creamy and they feel so luxurious. The shade range is gorgeous. I just really feel like these are a standout blush in my collection right now. You can apply them straight to the skin and blend them out. You can warm them up on the back of your hand if you want more of a soft and diffused look. Another shade I really love is the shade Petal. It's kind of similar but a little bit more mauvey, I would say.

Like, do you guys see how that just blended out so nicely into my skin and how pretty this color is? I used my Makeup by Mario F4 brush, I've been loving this one for blush. But look at that, and it's very buildable. Usually when I'm in a rush I will just like apply it straight from the stick and I'll leave it at that, but I'll show you guys right now really quickly how buildable these blushes are. Just pushing that into the skin, blends so quickly. Look at that. So easy to use, so forgiving. You almost like can't overdo these blushes. But look, I just think one of the most beautiful blushes I've tried in a very long time.

## Brightening with Concealer

Moving on to concealer, I'm using the Armani Luminous Silk Concealer. This is just one of my favorite concealers and it has been for for quite a while. I do find that this isn't like a super, super full coverage concealer, it's definitely more of like a medium natural coverage, which I like. But I also really appreciate that it doesn't really pill on my under eyes or really anywhere on my face because it's got a very thin, airy consistency. It just isn't heavy and it doesn't bunch up, so it's a huge reason why I like this one for every day. And I like to blend out that concealer using my Kevyn Aucoin concealer brush.

## Setting Cream Products with Spray

So usually after I apply all my creams, I like to set my face just to kind of help marinate things a little bit while I'm doing the eyes. So I'm going to go in with my Charlotte Tilbury Airbrush Flawless Setting Spray. I really do find that it helps my makeup last all day and it just like melts everything together so nicely.

## Simple & Bright Everyday Eyes

Moving on to eyes, I've been keeping it so simple and I love it. ## Setting & Layering with Powders

Moving right along, I'm going to set my under eyes. I'm using the Pat McGrath Skin Fetish Sublime Perfection Blurring Under Eye Powder in the baby pink shade.
